ratings_why.fun: Every turn asks where news starts and who stands next to whom, and Wendelin, ties and the Huddle reach into other tribes' cards in ways the builds don't even list.
ratings_why.distinct: Halving spread along a tie-able graph plays unlike any tribe today, though growth along the touching run overlaps Hedgerow's home turf.

verdict_why: One real unclear rule on the Thirty-Two decides whether fight Gossip becomes permanent; the rest is ready.

points.text: Say whether "heard last turn" includes the fight. If it does, Speaker Brotkrume's in-fight Gossip comes back as a permanent re-broadcast next turn, which is a very different card.
Roll-Caller counts Rats, which pulls against the mixed-Knot pitch; counting every unit in the Knot would reward the odd boards the tribe is selling.
Let Cold-Shed Litter tie its Stray to itself, so the Tier 1 already teaches ties and the Stray can plug a far gap.
The Huddle's shares counting as hits makes a Bristle neighbour punish every share; a Rat with Bristle at Tier 3 or 4 would let Rats find that combo on their own.

standouts.why: Turns any other tribe's growth into news, so Pass, Eat and spells all become Rat inputs.
Ties count for every card's touching, so one tie bends Hedgerow runs, Chimney doubling and the Alderman's tribe count at once.
Turns Bristle, Shield and Damage Reduction from other tribes into a multi-hit defence engine.

weakest.why: A plain two-body tempo card with no Knot decision after it's played.
One obvious job: count Rats and Gossip at Start of Combat.
Gold on Hears is fine but adds no positional choice.

flags.note: Whether fight gains count as heard "last turn" is unstated.
Speaker next to Mill-Chimney with We, the Rattenkönig gives every unit the biggest unit's full stats each fight.
Wendelin beside an Ooze that eats a big unit is one huge Gossip that Ilse then repeats.
Bristle triggers once per share, so a Bristle neighbour can kill attackers fast.
